rationale: Highest grid-only score among 14 admissible feasible candidates (7.50): conventional restoration maximises restored electrical energy and never interrupts customers who still have supply.

7 feasible plan(s) that interrupt supplied customers for voltage headroom (e.g. C35: Close SW-18-33 · open SW-31-32 · shed B8) are outside this policy.
Restores 472 kW at switching; nothing shed; 2 switching operation(s).
PU-2 stays without supply: the extended-period simulation shows critical-facility pressure falling to 0.0 m from 18:12 and tank storage to 0%.

The encirra optimum (C16: Close SW-25-29 · shed B30) restores 554 kW; with it critical-facility pressure stays ≥ 37.8 m (tank minimum 47%). In grid-only accounting it is worth 7.45 MWh against 7.60 MWh for this plan.

assumptions: Synthetic district on the IEEE 33-bus benchmark; ratings, pump curves and demand profiles are declared assumptions.

A pump runs only if its bus is energised and V ≥ 0.90 pu (latching undervoltage trip).
Switching is executed remotely at the switching time; the faulted section stays isolated for the horizon.
Gensets carry essential electrical load only; they do not power pumping stations.
Grid-only objective: maximise restored electrical energy; facilities on backup generation count as served; pumps are ordinary loads; water ignored.
